text: Welcome to Reports and Dashboards. Before you build a single report, Salesforce makes you choose a report type, and that one choice controls everything you can do afterward. This lesson is about understanding that choice before you ever touch the Report Builder.

A report type is the template: it defines the primary object and which related objects and fields a report is allowed to show. A standard report type ships with Salesforce for common combinations, like Opportunities or Accounts. A custom report type is one an admin builds, for combinations Salesforce didn't anticipate. All three control access to data before you ever add a filter.

Here's a simple report built on the standard Accounts report type. Just account fields: name, type, nothing from related objects. That's the ceiling this report type puts on what the report can ever show.

Now compare that to a report on the Accounts with Opportunities report type. Same starting object, but now opportunity fields like Opportunity Name, Close Date, and Amount are available too, because the report type was built to expose that relationship. Nothing else changed, just the type.

This is the Fields pane while building a report. Notice the fields are grouped: Opportunity Information, Account General, Opportunity Custom Info, Account Custom Info. Every one of those groups exists because the report type decided to expose it. If a field isn't in one of these folders, it isn't available, full stop.

Custom report types let an admin choose, for each relationship, with or with-or-without the related object, an inner join or a left join in SQL terms. Pick the report type carefully, because changing it later usually means rebuilding the report. Next up: actually creating one.
